title: Ski and sun holidays: when one of you wants snow and one wants sun
author: Matt
intro: One of you has been dreaming of fresh powder since October. The other wants to sit somewhere warm with a book and never see a ski boot. You don't have to take turns. There are a handful of places in and around Europe where a warm city or coast sits an hour or two below a ski area, so you can split the day and meet for dinner.
seo_title: Ski and sun holidays: snow and warmth on one trip
seo_description: Places where one of you can ski and the other can stay warm: Granada and Sierra Nevada, Nice and Isola 2000, Cyprus and Marrakech. Compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Best all-rounder:** Granada and Sierra Nevada
- **Best skiing:** Nice and Isola 2000
- **Warmest base:** Marrakech, about 20°C
- **Snow most reliable:** Jan to March

The warm-side temperatures are average February highs from our guides, and journey times are typical drives in good conditions. Mountain roads close and snow varies a lot from year to year at the southern resorts, so check the resort's own snow report and road conditions before you go.

sections.heading: The four best pairings compared
sections.text:
| Warm base | February high | Ski area | Drive from the base |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Granada](/destinations/granada) | 15°C | Sierra Nevada | about 45 to 60 min |
| [Nice](/destinations/nice) | 14°C | Isola 2000 | about 1½ hrs |
| [Limassol](/destinations/limassol) | 18°C | Troodos | about 1 hr |
| [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) | 20°C | Oukaïmeden | about 1½ to 2 hrs |

The catch is that the closer the skiing is to real warmth, the smaller and less reliable it tends to be. Granada and Nice are the safest bets for proper skiing. Cyprus and Morocco are more about the novelty of skiing in the morning and eating outside in the sun that evening.

sections.heading: Granada and Sierra Nevada: the best all-rounder
sections.text:
[Granada](/destinations/granada) is the easiest place to make this work. The Sierra Nevada ski resort at Pradollano is only about 30 to 40 km from the city, a drive of roughly 45 minutes to an hour, and buses run up from Granada's bus station in the ski season, though only a few times a day. The slopes go well above 3,000 metres, so the season usually runs from around December into April.

The non-skier gets one of Spain's great cities: the Alhambra, the old Albaicín quarter, a free tapa with most drinks in many bars, and around 15°C on a sunny February afternoon. It's cool rather than beach weather, but it's often sunny and dry.

Tip: book Alhambra tickets weeks ahead, even in winter. They sell out, and they're the one thing the non-skier will most want to do.

Most people fly to [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), which has direct flights from most UK airports, then drive about an hour and a half to Granada. If the skier fancies one day in the mountains and the rest by the sea, Málaga itself is around 18°C in February.

sections.heading: Nice and Isola 2000: the best skiing
sections.text:
If the skier in your group wants a proper resort, the Côte d'Azur is the answer. Isola 2000 is about 90 km from Nice airport, roughly an hour and a half by car, and a ski bus runs up from Nice and the airport in winter.

- **For the skier:** a full-size, purpose-built resort, far bigger than the ski areas in Cyprus or Morocco.
- **For the sun-seeker:** [Nice](/destinations/nice) at around 14°C, with the Promenade des Anglais, the old town's markets and lunch outside on a sunny day.
- **Getting there:** Nice has direct flights from many UK airports, about two hours from London.

It's the coolest of the four warm bases, so think of it as a bright city break with blue skies rather than winter sun. February usually brings the Nice Carnival and Menton's lemon festival, which is a good reason for the non-skier to be there.

sections.heading: Cyprus and Marrakech: the novelty options
sections.text:
These two have the warmest bases but the least dependable snow:

- **Cyprus:** the small ski area on Mount Olympus in the Troodos mountains is about an hour's drive from [Limassol](/destinations/limassol). It has only a handful of lifts, and the season usually runs from early January to late March, snow permitting. Meanwhile, Limassol and [Paphos](/destinations/paphos) are around 17 to 18°C. Our [Malta or Cyprus in winter](/blog/malta-or-cyprus-in-winter) post covers the island in more detail.
- **Morocco:** Oukaïmeden sits at about 2,600 metres in the High Atlas, an hour and a half to two hours from [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech). It's very basic by Alpine standards, and some winters have little snow, but skiing in the Atlas and being back in a 20°C city for dinner is hard to beat as a story.

Watch out: don't book either trip just for the skiing. Treat the snow as a bonus day, and choose the place because the warm side of the trip works for both of you.

sections.heading: Other ways to share the week
sections.text:
If none of those pairings appeal, a few other set-ups work well:

- **Split the week:** four nights in the Alps and three in the sun. Geneva and the Canaries both have plenty of UK flights, so it can work with one extra flight.
- **Pick a sunny ski resort with a good town:** someone who doesn't ski can still enjoy long lunches on sunny terraces, spas and walks. Our [best ski resorts for a weekend](/blog/best-ski-resorts-for-a-weekend-from-the-uk) post includes resorts with real towns.
- **Take turns:** snow this February, sun next winter, and write the deal down so no one forgets.

Our [ski holidays](/destinations/ski-holidays) page lists resorts by month, and [when everyone wants a different holiday](/blog/when-everyone-wants-a-different-holiday) has more ways to find a compromise.

sections.heading: Deciding together
sections.text:
The hardest part is usually working out how much each of you actually cares. Is it skiing every day or just a taste of snow? Is it real heat or just blue skies?

Try putting the four pairings, plus a straight ski trip and a straight sun trip, on a shared list in somewhere.party. Give each of you points to spread across them. If the points end up close, let the draw pick, and at least no one had to win the argument.

faqs.question: Where in Europe can you ski and have warm weather on the same holiday?
faqs.answer: Granada is the best known, with the Sierra Nevada ski resort about an hour from a city that's around 15°C in February. Nice with Isola 2000 is better for skiing, while Cyprus and Marrakech have warmer bases but smaller, less reliable ski areas.

faqs.question: How far is Sierra Nevada from Granada?
faqs.answer: The resort is about 30 to 40 km from Granada, a drive of around 45 minutes to an hour. Buses run from Granada's bus station in the ski season, but only a few times a day.

faqs.question: Can you really ski in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, on Mount Olympus in the Troodos mountains, about an hour from Limassol. It's a small area with a few lifts, and the season usually runs from early January to late March, depending on snow.

faqs.question: Can you ski near Marrakech?
faqs.answer: Yes, at Oukaïmeden in the High Atlas, about an hour and a half to two hours away. It's basic, and snow varies a lot from year to year, so treat it as a one-day adventure rather than a ski holiday.
